National Weather Service Burlington VT
226 AM EDT Fri Oct 30 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
As of 224 AM EDT Friday...

No significant changes have been made to the forecast.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
As of 224 AM EDT Friday...

1. Some lingering showers and cooler weather is expected across 
the region today following a cold front. Mostly dry and seasonable 
conditions are expected through the weekend into the start of next 
week. 

2. Increased fire weather concerns through this weekend. 

3. Two fronts with little moisture or forcing will offer low 
end chances for rain early next week, before becoming dry and warm.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 224 AM EDT Friday...

KEY MESSAGE 1: The cold front continues to move through the region this 
morning, with dwindling rain showers and plentiful cloud cover along 
with it. Rainfall amounts with this feature have generally been a 
few hundredths, although some locations across northern New York 
have observed a few tenths on an inch of rain. Strong cold air 
advection will take place behind the front today, with increased 
clouds and some chances for some lingering showers in the favored 
upslope areas with some flurries possible in the higher terrain. 
Temperatures on Friday will be more seasonable compared to 
yesterday, with highs in the upper 40s and 50s. 

Heading into the weekend and the start of next week, surface high 
pressure looks to build into the region once again. This will lead 
to another stretch of dry weather, with ample sunshine, light winds, 
and pleasant conditions to round out October and welcome the start 
of November. Temperatures on Saturday will be a little on the cooler 
side, with highs generally in the mid 40s to low 50s, moderating 
towards the start of next week.

KEY MESSAGE 2: Breezy winds and lower relative humidity values will 
lead to increased fire weather concerns over the next few days, 
especially given the plentiful dry leaf litter across the area 
serving as fuel. Wind gusts today and Friday will generally be in 
the 15 to 25 mph range, with some higher gusts are possible. Minimum 
relative humidity values will generally be between 40 to 55 percent 
for today. Heading into the weekend, minimum relative humidity 
values should drop into the 30 to 45 percent range, but winds look 
to be much lighter. Recent rainfall amounts remain rather 
negligible, with most locations only receiving a few hundredths of 
an inch, but a few locations across northern New York received over 
0.1 inches of rain with these showers. Cloud cover across the region 
today will help limit some of these fire weather concerns.

KEY MESSAGE 3: There remains little change to the details regarding a 
frontal boundary expected to shift southwards Monday night into 
Tuesday. Upper level vorticity will shift east, and an incoming 
ridge will help dissipate the front. It's very possible it does not 
even make it to the international border, but a handful of scenarios 
depict it reaching at least far northern Vermont. For late Tuesday 
into Wednesday, a surface low will lift from the Plains north 
towards James Bay. It will send a warm front into the region. Better 
moisture and dynamics will remain well to our north and west as 
surface high pressure moving from far eastern Canada into the 
maritimes will keep stable, southeasterly flow filtering into the 
region. Again, some rain could develop with a handful of forecast 
scenarios depicting light rain along the international border.

Thereafter, the large scale pattern amplifies. The NBM is only 
forecasting lower 60s, but 925mb temperatures ranging from 10-13 C 
suggest that some upper 60s could be in the cards. Overall, there's 
still spread in terms of the evolution of a compact upper low across 
the Plains, and how it interacts with a rich moisture plume off the 
Atlantic, but the timing is looking more consistent with an arrival 
of next Thursday night into Friday. This could be a very soaking 
rain. The NBM mean ranges from 0.50-1.00", but the overall pattern 
suggests we could see more. Seeing long range guidance with 1" 
probabilities of 25-40% and 2" probabilities of 5-15% certainly 
suggest some potential for a little more. We'll have plenty of time 
to monitor the evolution of this feature.

&&

.AVIATION /06Z FRIDAY THROUGH TUESDAY/...
Through 06Z Saturday...A weak cold front is moving southeast across
the region. Light rain showers extend from about Newcomb, NY
northeast towards Morrisville, VT as of 150am. Some MVFR ceilings
will likely settle into KSLK and KEFK. It's not impossible that
KBTV, KRUT, and KMSS could observe some ceilings around 2500-3000 ft
agl as well, but thinking most terminals will remain around
3000-5000 ft agl for much of the next 24 hours. Southwest or
variable flow will become west to west- northwest over the next 6
hours, and accelerate after 14Z. Additional troughs will settle
through the area, the first passing southeast around 10Z-14Z. Most
will not observe precipitation, except perhaps KSLK, but it will
reinforce the borderline MVFR ceilings. It will bring wind speeds
and gusts upwards towards 9-14 knots sustained with gusts 16-25
knots possible. Another will shift southeast about 22Z-03Z, which
will then bring a more appreciable shift to northwest winds and
could keep sustained winds from totally dropping off. It should
still gradually subside, and then clouds will begin to lift and
scatter behind this last trough.

Outlook...

Saturday: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Saturday Night: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Sunday: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Sunday Night: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Monday: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Monday Night: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Tuesday: VFR. Slight chance SHRA.

&&

.MARINE...
As of 224 AM EDT Friday...

A Lake Wind Advisory is in effect for today. After a lull in winds 
this morning, northwesterly winds will increase throughout the day, 
between the 15-25 KT range, with gusts closer to 30 knots. 
Waves will generally build to 2-4 feet towards this evening. 
Winds are expected to gradually diminish overnight tonight into
Saturday morning.

&&

.BTV WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
VT...None.
NY...None.

&&
